🌽🇲🇽 <u>MAYA COMMUNITIES WIN: PROBE THE GLYPHOSATE IN OUR WATER</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court unanimously sided with 17 Maya communities in Hopelchén, Campeche, ordering SEMARNAT, CONAGUA and COFEPRIS to investigate glyphosate contamination in their water. The court set a precautionary standard rooted in Indigenous rights: "the State cannot wait for absolute scientific certainty about possible environmental damage before beginning prevention." The communities first sued back in 2020.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE COURT TO THE OPPOSITION: YOU'RE NOT MEXICO</u>

Mexico's electoral court (TEPJF) ordered the new right-wing party "Somos México" to drop its name, logo and colors by Aug 31, ruling that claiming to be Mexico amounts to a "symbolic appropriation of national identity" — no single faction gets to brand itself as the whole nation. The party says it will comply "under protest," calling it an "outrage." Sheinbaum backed the ruling: a party is not the country.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>PAN EX-GOVERNOR'S FUEL-THEFT EMPIRE UNRAVELS</u>

Mexico's FGR found two hidden Mexico City warehouses tied to Ernesto Ruffo Appel — the PAN's first-ever governor — full of import permits and contracts that simulated a fuel-smuggling ring moving stolen gasoline from the US. Ruffo and 24 others are under investigation; nine are already jailed. The man the right sold as its clean-government pioneer now anchors the huachicol fiscal probe.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S FORMAL JOBS HIT STATE RECORDS</u>

Formal employment is breaking state records: Baja California led the country with 7% annual growth and 70,993 new jobs, Oaxaca followed at 5.8%, and San Luis Potosí reached 497,652 insured workers — its highest since IMSS records began in 1997 — El Economista reports. Platform-based jobs jumped 86.6% year-on-year, and the average base wage just hit an all-time high of 673.9 pesos a day.

🇲🇽💉 <u>CDMX BEAT MEASLES: 4.4M SHOTS, CASES DOWN 99%</u>

Mexico City drove measles down 99% from its peak of ~80 weekly cases, applying 4.4 million vaccines over a year — 2,500 vaccinators, 150 mobile sites, once nearly 60,000 doses in a single day. "In Mexico City we contained, stopped measles and made it retreat," said Mayor Clara Brugada, calling it "public health turned into organized solidarity."
